source_text: 'By marriage, the husband and wife are one person in law: that is, the very being or legal existence of the woman is suspended during the marriage, or at least is incorporated and consolidated into that of the husband: under whose wing, protection, and cover, she performs every thing; and is therefore called ... a feme-covert.' He cannot grant anything to her or covenant with her, she cannot sue in her own name, and 'the husband is bound to provide his wife with necessaries by law'. Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, ch. 15 (Oxford: Clarendon, 1765). Passage checked at https://wams.nyhistory.org/colonies-and-revolution/english-colonies/coverture/
notes: Care + control: the husband both maintains (R2, provides_care h w) and may chastise/restrain (R5, can_sanction h w) the same subject. That is the sub-signature matched against police-crisis and cps; the wife's own labour (R3) is implicit and runs the other way (provides_care w h), which is why care_and_sanction_same_role is restricted to care received by is_subject, and why care_assigned_by_sex is 'violated' rather than 'holds' (the husband's maintenance also counts as care). Pitfalls: (1) an encoder that drops R3 loses the household-labour strand and reports the wife as purely a recipient of care; (2) R4 and R7 are disabilities (or_else null) and should not be lowered as sanctioned prohibitions; (3) no_standing is 'reachable' not 'holds_to_k' because before marry() the woman has standing (feme sole); the iso with the animal entries on 'cannot sue in own name' holds only post-marriage and is structural, not a claim of equal status. Rival reading: equity courts' separate estates (not encoded) gave propertied wives a partial exit from R1; recorded here, not in the rules. ADR 0009: R2 and R3 are state obligations (must-be provides_care); as per-step action obligations they filled the one action slot at every married step and made marriage unsatisfiable (care_assigned_by_sex held vacuously). Slice 2 root change (2026-11-06, plans/priority-slice2.md section 5), inherited by the coverture family: action draw_subsistence(w) (no effects, not a default capacity) and derived fluent has_own_income(w) := (enabled draw_subsistence w), declared for the floor route (coverture-floor R20). No rule names the action here, so it is unregulated and has_own_income is false, as hold_property and keep_earnings are under coverture.

notes: The same role (officer) is bound to care (R2, assess) and empowered to detain (R3) and use force (R5): care_and_sanction_same_role. subject_cannot_exit is reachable with scope=interaction only (the 72-hour hold), not institution; report the scope. Pitfalls: (1) R1 is the implicit rule that makes this police-crisis rather than crisis-team; the statute itself also names mobile crisis teams as holders of the 5150 power, so an encoder reading only the statute will not see why armed officers are the ones who come; (2) a trivial encoding that ignores or_else on R4 will cluster this with crisis-team (plan: worked pitfall); (3) no_standing is unreachable_open, not 'safe': the subject keeps has_standing via R8, but the bound k=6 says nothing beyond it. Armed status (R6) is a tying strand: it is not required by 5150 and is what the crisis-team reform removes. ADR 0009: R2 is a state obligation ('on an ongoing basis' is a state); R1 stays an action obligation but dispatch consumes the call. Exogenous triggers (call_received, in_crisis, danger, resists) are initial_free, since under init=declared a fluent no action sets would otherwise be pinned false and no call could ever arrive. Re-encoded 2026-11-06 to WIC 5150 (plans/sourcing.md, L1 landing): the care duty (R2) and a custody power (R11) are the facility's; the officer keeps detain (R3, now detain(o, f, s), delivering to a facility) and force (R5), so care_and_sanction_same_role is violated here (a second sanctioner) while the care+control form holds with the facility as the bundled role. source_text: From memory, NOT a verified quotation (the page could not be opened from this session): the experiment ran online groups of 20-30 participants who, in randomly paired rounds, each proposed a name for a pictured object and were paid a small reward when the two names matched and charged a small penalty when they did not; once a group had converged on one name, a committed minority instructed to use a different name was added, and minorities of about 25% of the group overturned the established name while smaller ones (around 20% and below) did not. The abstract (as recalled) reports 'direct empirical demonstration of the existence of a tipping point in the dynamics of changing social conventions' and that minority groups that reached the critical mass 'were consistently able to overturn the established behavior'. Centola, Becker, Brackbill & Baronchelli, 'Experimental evidence for tipping points in social convention', Science 360(6393):1116-1119, 8 June 2018, doi:10.1126/science.aas8827. notes: Calibration / control entry for layer-2 gate (b) (plans/layer2-abm.md; philengine/abm/gate.py crit_b reads id `naming-convention`, the payoffs-block key `committed_action`, parameter `committed_minority`; the property `new_convention_adopted` was its placeholder reading until engine slice 4, see the drift note). A pure coordination game, not a liberation case: no subject, no care, no sanction, no exit; the only question it serves is whether the coordination module's tipping location emerges from the sweep rather than from a constant. committed_minority: share of agents holding `use_new` regardless of payoff; Centola's observed tipping band ~ 25%: largest failing minority ~21%, smallest succeeding ~25% (UNVERIFIED, from memory; reworded 2026-11-04 per the encoding review finding 9 from 'between 21% and 31%', 31% being the largest minority tested, not the band's edge). Recorded here, not asserted by the model. Payoffs (A1): both actions 1.0, because the coordination module pays only on matching, so the payoff IS the matching reward and the two names are symmetric; the gate sweeps committed_minority, not payoffs. Rules: two `may` with condition true (ADR 0015 A6 strict enabledness: every action needs a may) and no must or must_not (the game has no sanction: a mismatch forgoes the reward, it breaks no rule). Fluents: `uses_old` / `uses_new` are two fluents rather than one, because the ABM's state is role-level and shared (A2 deferred) and `Reference.successor` lets set-true win over set-false, so when members fire both names in one step both atoms are true; the property therefore asks for new-and-not-old, which on the shared state reads 'some member fired use_new and no member fired use_old this step', i.e. the convention has switched. `initial: (uses_old member)` records the established convention at layer 1. The payoffs block also carries the three RESERVED keys the engine's slice-4 coordination module reads (philengine/abm/model.py RESERVED_PAYOFF_KEYS, ASSUMED, added by the engine agent concurrently on 2026-11-04 after the first material-only run here showed the agents bootstrapping practice from a payoff tie by rng and ignoring `initial`): `coordinated: [use_old, use_new]` (both names are assurance-gated: a name pays only when the agent's same-role neighbour share of it meets its threshold), `committed_action: use_new` (what the committed_minority holds whatever it pays), `initial_practice: use_old` (every uncommitted member starts on the old name, so an established convention exists for the minority to tip). These keys are hand inputs, like the numbers (A1); nothing in them names a tipping location. Layer 2 with the coordination module (information, not a dataset verdict; written before the first (b) run): some adjacent pair of sweep points 0.05..0.50 is expected to show an adoption jump > 0.5 (crit_b PASS) and the location is NOT preregistered: the gate's own point is that the dataset records Centola's band and the model does not assert it. DRIFT, recorded not edited (2026-11-04, after the run): the engine's slice-4 crit_b no longer reads `new_convention_adopted` (its review finding 6: a property mean cannot express a population share under shared role state) but the member role's last-step share of `committed_action`; at 30 seeds that share by committed_minority 0.05..0.50 is [0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.35, 0.54, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.97]: equal to the committed share through 0.20 (no uncommitted member converts), above it from 0.25 on, so the tipping begins at the 0.20 -> 0.25 boundary, inside Centola's band, but the curve is graded and the max adjacent jump is 0.19, not > 0.5: crit_b FAIL under both coordination configurations. The location was not set by the dataset (the entry carries no threshold); whether the sharpness criterion, the threshold draw U(0, threshold_max) or the 20-agent graph is what grades the curve is an engine question, not a dataset one. `new_convention_adopted` stays the layer-1 property (reachable, as preregistered) and an information line at layer 2. Negative control in spirit: it is listed in CONTROLS (`not_isomorphic_to_control` on the three care+control cluster members, ADR 0007 / ADR 0013) because it must match nothing: PREREGISTERED none@guard+strands against coverture-household, police-crisis and cps (no must, no rival may, no subject). source_text: 'Female footbinding in China lasted for 1,000 years but ended in a single generation. I show that each practice is a self-enforcing convention, in Schelling's (1960) sense, maintained by interdependent expectations on the marriage market.' 'A Schelling coordination diagram explains how the three methods of the Chinese campaign to abolish footbinding succeeded in bringing it to a quick end.' 'The convention hypothesis predicts that promotion of such pledge associations would help bring female genital mutilation to an end.' (Mackie 1996, abstract, via a search-index snippet 2026-11-04; the article was not opened.) Pledge associations: members pledged not to bind their daughters' feet and not to let their sons marry women with bound feet (Wikipedia 'Tian Zu Hui' / 'Heavenly Foot Society', snippets, [R]). plans/layer2-abm.md records these sources as opened on 2026-11-03 by the planning session; this entry's encoder could not reopen them on 2026-11-04.
notes: Layer-2 gate (a) institution. Mackie's convention: a family binds because every other family binds and suitors expect it (R3 sanctioned norm, R5 the market's refusal, R6/R7 the marriage condition); the campaign's pledge associations (R4) create a marriage pool in which an unbound daughter is marriageable, so the sanction R5 lapses for pledged families and leave_unbound (R2) becomes costless once enough neighbours pledge. Deviations from the task sketch: no matchmaker/community role (no source gives one a rule); a `suitor` role instead, because the sanction needs an actor and Mackie's sanction is the other side of the market; the pledge's son half is a second pledge action R10 accept_match_pledge (suitor) read by R5/R6 (until 2026-11-04 it was folded into the family's pledge; encoding review finding 2); marriageable is derived (ADR 0013) from R7 rather than asserted; R3 is unconditional and R5 carries the (not pledged) condition, so that the pledge changes nothing at layer 1 (the preregistration the gate pair needs). Sources: every text was read as a search snippet, none as a page (network closed in this session); the abstract sentences are verbatim from the index, everything else is [R] or UNVERIFIED and says so per rule. PREREGISTERED (2026-11-04, before any run; layer 1 under init declared, strict compliance, step one): binding_practised PERSISTS in footbinding AND in footbinding-no-pledge (bound(daughter) is initial; the only action that clears it, leave_unbound, is forbidden by the sanctioned norm R3, which strict compliance never breaches; the pledge R4 changes nothing at layer 1 because the norm R3 is unconditional and only the sanction R5 reads pledged). marriage_requires_binding HOLDS_TO_K in both (R7 is the only marry_off rule and its condition is bound-or-pledged; non-vacuous because marriageable(family, daughter) is true at t=0). subject_cannot_exit and dependent_cannot_exit REACHABLE in both (t=0: is_subject(daughter) and R9 bars refuse_binding). The pair's layer-1 verdicts are IDENTICAL (minimal_pair_of.differs_on is null on purpose: the pair differs only at layer 2). Expected warnings: can_sanction, provides_care, has_standing, can_claim_for undeclared (no care or standing here); care_and_sanction_same_role is not expected (it would be vacuous: no provides_care). Isomorphism: not_isomorphic_to the care+control cluster (no carer, no sanctioner over a cared-for subject; the sanction here is a counterparty's refusal); isomorphic_to nothing (no entry has the convention shape). Information only, not an expectation: under --compliance sanctioned binding_practised should FAIL in both (leave_unbound may fire and pay the sanction). PREREGISTERED (2026-11-04, encoding review finding 2, written and committed before the first run with the suitor pledge): adding accept_match_pledge(suitor, daughter) [effect pledged(suitor)] with rule R10 suitor may accept_match_pledge, and reading (pledged suitor) in R5 (and-not) and R6 (or), changes NO layer-1 verdict in footbinding or footbinding-no-pledge: binding_practised persists, marriage_requires_binding holds_to_k, subject_cannot_exit and dependent_cannot_exit reachable in both; the new pledge only lifts the sanction R5 (and widens R6), R3 is unconditional, R7 is untouched, and pledged is a fluent per role (footbinding-no-pledge strips BOTH pledge actions and both pledge rules R4 and R10, so nothing sets pledged(suitor) there). Iso: still none at every level against the care+control cluster; isomorphic_to nothing. Expected warnings unchanged (can_sanction, provides_care, has_standing, can_claim_for undeclared). Layer 2 (information, not an expectation): pledged(suitor) is role-level too (A2), so one suitor's pledge lifts R5 for every suitor, the same coarseness as pledged(family): the A2 caveat now applies on both sides; gate (a)'s _has_pledges reading is unchanged (true via either pledge) and ablate_pledges strips both. If any verdict flips, the drift is recorded here and the expectations are not edited. RESULT (2026-11-04, after the run, commit b6f48aa preceding it): no drift. check-all 115/115 with all four verdicts as preregistered in both entries; `phil rules gate` PASS; pytest 15 passed; no warning printed for either entry (none was printed before the change either). Layer 1 has one cohort (encoding review 2026-11-04 finding 4): one daughter, bound at t=0, and `married` never clears, so no trace shows a per-cohort binding decision before the market; a `new_cohort` action clearing bound/married is deferred to the author. LAYER 2 (for the engine's coordination module, which is a stub at writing): the actions the module should treat as `coordinated` are bind and leave_unbound (a family's choice pays only when enough neighbouring families choose the same, Mackie's marriage-market assurance game); the pledge is leave_unbound_pledge (A3 naming convention, counts as adoption of leave_unbound for neighbours' thresholds). philengine has no action tag for this yet (ActionDecl has no `tags`), so the entry carries an ASSUMED extra field `coordinated: [bind, leave_unbound]` that pydantic ignores.
